scope: Continue the current Triggerword-5 P0 frontier by atomizing stern.py effect admission/outcome correlation, distinguishing declared EffectGate semantics from actual enforcement, cross-checking Claude Code parallel-hook semantics, and producing Frankenstein-2.0 repair deltas without modifying or executing the donor.

atoms.what_it_does: zulassen() evaluates capability, session generation, file preconditions and an idempotency marker, then persists ZUGELASSEN/ABGELEHNT/WIEDERHOLUNG/UNGEPRUEFT into effects; the same source explicitly states this bookkeeping path and leases never block the tool and that an older external wache-koenig.py is the separate blocking watcher.
atoms.why_it_exists: Provide bounded request-side effect bookkeeping and later result reconciliation without letting hook bookkeeping stall the interactive session.
dependencies: external historical wache-koenig.py for actual blocking, according to current source commentary
atoms.failure_mode: A consumer may mistake the EffectGate name or ABGELEHNT status for enforced denial even though the tool is allowed to proceed.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Admission stores only one effect_id per session rather than one per tool call.
atoms.privacy_implication: tool_input-derived target/argv cross the durable journal boundary; current source applies redaction before persistence.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: PreToolUse path is designed for a 0.4s internal budget and fails silent.
atoms.state_lifetime: durable effect row plus session-scoped mutable pointer
known_counterevidence: No runtime hook was fired in this Triggerword-5 run; this is exact-current source evidence, not a runtime receipt.
open_questions: Recover and inspect the external historical blocker/wache-koenig lineage before deciding which enforcement checks are donor-worthy.

atoms.what_it_does: zulassen() writes each new effect_id into active_turns.effect_id keyed only by session_id; merken() later reads that same single session field to choose which effects row receives the PostToolUse outcome. The donor does not bind this path to a per-call tool_use_id.
atoms.why_it_exists: Reuse the existing active_turns session row as a lightweight PreToolUse-to-PostToolUse bridge.
outputs: chosen effects row for outcome update
dependencies: assumption that one session-scoped mutable pointer is sufficient to correlate tool lifecycle events
atoms.failure_mode: Overlapping or reordered tool calls can overwrite the session pointer and attach an outcome to the wrong request; a failed/missing later PreToolUse can also leave a stale prior pointer available to PostToolUse.
atoms.concurrency_implication: High: official Claude Code hook semantics expose tool_use_id per call and document concurrent PostToolUse firing for parallel tool calls, so one mutable effect_id per session is not a safe general correlation key.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: The current shortcut is cheap but loses per-call identity.
atoms.state_lifetime: mutable for the active session and not cleared in the inspected effect-completion path
tests_or_receipts: External-primary cross-check: current Claude Code hooks documentation describes tool_use_id on hook payloads and concurrent PostToolUse for parallel tool calls.
known_counterevidence: If a particular host disabled all parallel tool execution, this race could be latent there; the donor source does not encode such a serialization invariant.
open_questions: Add an executable two-parallel-call regression in the Triggerword-4 assembly lane; do not use runtime absence of a race as proof unless per-call identity is asserted and checked.

atoms.what_it_does: _wirkung_pruefen() derives a compact post-execution observation: Bash uses exit status/error state and hashes output; file-changing tools hash the post-call target bytes when present; other results hash a bounded response representation.
atoms.why_it_exists: Turn PostToolUse into evidence about what execution returned or what file bytes exist after the call without persisting the entire raw result.
reads: target file bytes for file tools
atoms.failure_mode: A successful process exit or resulting file hash proves an observed execution result at that scope, not that the request was authorized or that the external world effect is semantically correct.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Safe only if attached to the correct per-call effect identity.
atoms.privacy_implication: Hashes reduce raw-response persistence, but upstream journal fields still require redaction.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Local hashing can be bounded for normal files but may become expensive on very large target files unless size policy is explicit.
known_counterevidence: This Triggerword-5 run did not reexecute the verifier.
open_questions: Define size-bounded and external-effect-specific outcome verifiers rather than treating one generic success bit as complete effect verification.

atoms.what_it_does: merken() updates an existing ZUGELASSEN row to VERIFIED/FEHLGESCHLAGEN, preserves ABGELEHNT/WIEDERHOLUNG/UNGEPRUEFT labels when a row is found, but if no PreToolUse row is found it creates a new effects row directly as VERIFIED or FEHLGESCHLAGEN based on the observed result.
atoms.why_it_exists: Keep the journal non-empty even when request-side bookkeeping timed out or failed.
outputs: updated or newly inserted effects row
atoms.failure_mode: The word VERIFIED can mean successful observed execution even when no admission decision existed; authorization and outcome therefore collapse into one status vocabulary and can be misread downstream.
atoms.concurrency_implication: A stale non-null effect pointer can suppress the intended no-PreToolUse fallback and update an older row instead; this is a source-derived inference requiring a targeted regression.
atoms.privacy_implication: PostToolUse event memory persists redacted input and response summaries.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Fail-silent design favors continuity over guaranteed request-side journal completeness.
known_counterevidence: The fallback is useful as an observation record; the defect is semantic overloading, not the decision to preserve evidence.
open_questions: Split EffectRequest, EffectDecision and EffectOutcome identities/statuses so missing admission can remain ADMISSION_UNKNOWN while execution outcome is independently SUCCEEDED/FAILED/UNKNOWN.

atoms.what_it_does: Current source records a real prior failure where unfiltered tool_input/argv/target could persist secrets in effects/durable_memory, and implements defense-in-depth redaction before truncation/persistence for designated journal surfaces.
atoms.why_it_exists: Prevent canonical event/effect logs from becoming a plaintext secret sink while retaining enough metadata for debugging and provenance.
atoms.failure_mode: Pattern redaction is defense-in-depth, not proof that arbitrary secret formats cannot pass; logging raw payloads elsewhere would re-open the leak.
atoms.privacy_implication: Critical: redact before truncation and before any durable journal/memory write; prefer digests/typed fields over raw command/content payloads.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Local regex redaction is inexpensive relative to durable DB writes.
atoms.state_lifetime: privacy invariant for all durable effect/event records
tests_or_receipts: Current source comment classifies the historical leak as real/demonstrated; not independently reproduced in this run.
open_questions: Add structured secret-fence regressions covering request, decision, outcome, error and recovery journal paths in Frankenstein-2.0.

atoms.what_it_does: Routes PreToolUse and PostToolUse with matcher '*' to the same stern.py dispatcher for each tool call; the checked config contains no PostToolBatch route.
atoms.why_it_exists: Keep one lifecycle dispatcher and per-call effect bookkeeping.
atoms.failure_mode: Per-call fan-in is sound only when the dispatcher correlates each request/result with a stable per-call identity; session-only correlation is insufficient under parallel tool calls.
atoms.concurrency_implication: PostToolBatch could be useful for aggregate batch receipts, but must never replace per-tool decision/outcome identity or become a second effect authority.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: One subprocess per hook event preserves the existing bounded hook model but increases overlap likelihood under parallel calls.
known_counterevidence: Absence of PostToolBatch is not itself a defect; the defect is missing per-call correlation under documented parallel hooks.

hypotheses: Frankenstein-2.0 should retain the useful donor sequence request -> deterministic checks -> execution observation -> outcome re-entry, but implement it as three explicitly separate typed records: EffectRequest, EffectDecision and EffectOutcome.
Per-call tool_use_id plus session/generation/causal identity is the minimum safe correlation envelope for Claude Code effect lifecycles; a batch identifier may be additive but not a replacement.
The donor's post-call hashing is worth preserving as an outcome-evidence primitive after it is detached from authorization semantics.
counterhypotheses: A host-level configuration might serialize all state-changing tool calls and make the single active_turns.effect_id race unobservable in that deployment; current donor code does not encode or verify this assumption, while current Claude Code documentation explicitly supports parallel tool calls.

The historical external wache-koenig.py may already provide adequate true blocking enforcement for some tool classes; its exact source/reachability has not yet been recovered, so the present packet does not claim the entire deployed system had no blocker.
PostToolBatch might simplify aggregate reconciliation, but it cannot safely substitute for per-call identity because individual admission and outcomes can differ within one batch.
contradictions: EFFECT-NAME-VS-SEMANTICS: the donor labels this subsystem EffectGate and records ABGELEHNT, yet the exact source explicitly says this path never blocks tools; current EntityOS authority requires deterministic EffectGate/EffectJournal real-effect authority. Preserve the contradiction; do not carry the name forward as proof of enforcement.

PARALLEL-CORRELATION: donor effect completion correlates by one active_turns.effect_id per session, while current Claude Code hook semantics provide tool_use_id per call and document concurrent PostToolUse for parallel tool calls. These models are incompatible without an additional serialization invariant that is absent from the donor source.

STATUS-SEMANTICS: donor fallback can create VERIFIED from PostToolUse when no PreToolUse row exists. This preserves execution evidence but does not preserve admission evidence; Frankenstein-2.0 must not treat successful execution as retroactive authorization.

INGEST-LANE-MIGRATION: canonical main currently carries architecture_archaeology/TRIGGERWORD5_LIVE_FORENSIC_FEED while the newer owner branch carries frankenstein_architecture_ingest/inbox + INGEST_STATE. This packet stays in the mandated branch inbox and does not create a third lane.
critical_unknowns: Exact historical/current source and runtime reachability of the external wache-koenig blocker referenced by stern.py remain unresolved.
Exact Git chronology for first stern.py Phase-1 consolidation, first Phase-2 effect path, and later secret/idempotency repairs remains to be reconstructed.

The stale-pointer failure mode is strongly implied by the inspected source because active_turns.effect_id is reused and no clear is present in the inspected effect-completion path; an executable forced-PreToolUse-failure regression is still required before calling it runtime-reproduced.
